static_traits.name: Chen Zhiyuan
static_traits.family_status: Living alone in a house with a yard; parents once taught him to find inspiration; current relationship with family Not mentioned
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with friends, self-isolating out of fear of being judged; having a few close friends but finding it hard to open up
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems occurred before; has not received psychotherapy; no notable physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to self-Reflect, highly cooperative, Positive attitude; speed of speech and logical thinking details Not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: Since the dog passed away, I have felt incomplete and broken, which affects my ability to create art. Specifically, I struggle with perfectionism and harsh self-criticism.
basic_info.core_demands: Realizing that self-criticism and perfectionism are hindering my artistic expression and overall physical and mental health, thus seeking counseling to change these thinking and behavior patterns.
growth_experiences: The dog died a few months ago: its Death brought intense sadness and loss (self-reported 'feeling incomplete and broken'), with very high stress at the time; this subsequently triggered and worsened Perfectionism and harsh self-criticism, significantly affecting art creation and life rhythm.
Native family influence: the parents taught him to 'seek inspiration', providing early values and direction for his artistic pursuit.

Art growth experience: as a Self-study Artist, long self-improving and having felt proud after completing some works; however, recently when facing mistakes or imperfection in works, seeing them as failures, leading to Damaged self-confidence.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether my work is perfect

special_situations.event: Using the wrong green in a painting (the grass tone was off)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the work has a flaw, it means the whole work is a complete failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding continuing to create, or compulsively pursuing 'perfect revision' to avoid any mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This painting is completely ruined for me

special_situations.event: When mistakes or imperfection appear in art creation
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach extremely high standards, it proves I am not good enough, and not even worthy of commemorating my dog
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Setting overly high and rigid creative standards, constantly reproaching oneself, hoping to force oneself to achieve perfection
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will never make good works again

special_situations.event: When thinking that friends or others might evaluate my works
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the work is not perfect, others will judge me and look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduced socializing,Keeps distance from friends to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am terrible

special_situations.event: Trying to commemorate the deceased dog through creation, but the work has not yet reached the perfect standard in mind
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should commemorate it with a perfect work, otherwise it is a betrayal of it
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reproaching oneself with inner rules of 'must' 'should', continuously raising Demands, negating imperfect attempts

core_conflict.wish: Longs to maintain the emotional connection with the deceased dog through perfect artistic creation and gain confirmation of self-worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and imperfection will bring shame, judgment, even equating to 'letting down' and losing the meaning of important relationships
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and avoids the pain of failure through perfectionism and harsh self-criticism; reduces the risk of being evaluated by avoiding creative work and socializing

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough creator who may fail at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to lower standards, accept imperfection, or shift attention from results to process
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to understand 'lowering standards' as a betrayal of an important relationship (the memory of the dog) and a devaluation of self-worth
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a polite but firm tone, emphasizing the importance of perfection with moralizing 'should/must' language, emphasizing the legitimacy of commemoration, avoiding deep emotional experience.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When friends or the counselor invite deeper expression of vulnerable emotions and sad experiences
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Experiencing others' attention as potential judgment, believing that expressing vulnerability will lead to being looked down on or losing control
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Narrating with generalizing, abstract vocabulary, reducing emotional adjectives and details; restrained tone, remaining polite but not deep.

manifestations: Emotional support missing after the pet's death, feeling 'incomplete and broken'
Actively keeping distance from friends out of fear of being judged, Reduced socializing
outcomes: Declining motivation and enjoyment in artistic creation

manifestations: Making 'perfect creation' a necessary condition for commemoration and meaning-making; imperfect work is experienced as failure/loss of meaning
outcomes: Catastrophic and black-and-white interpretations of mistakes in creation further weaken the sense of meaning in life and creation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Demanding of oneself with 'should/must' to commemorate the dog with a perfect work
Seeing imperfection as unacceptable, negating positive experiences in the process

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism; harshly scrutinizes every detail in creating
Difficulty opening up to friends; worried about being judged

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not seeking outside help when support is needed, but turning to self-reproach and isolation
Substitutes self-criticism for outwardly expressing loss and sadness

positive_force: Having memories of experiencing pride and progress after completing a work, showing the capacity to learn and improve
Able to clearly identify and willing to change unhealthy thinking patterns such as catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking
Positive attitude, willing to try new creative methods (such as setting 30 minutes of non-judgmental practice daily)
Has a few trustworthy friends; has a potential support system
negative_force: Perfectionism and harsh self-criticism, binding self-worth to the perfection of the work
Catastrophizing and black-and-white thinking, quickly dragging the Overall evaluation to failure when mistakes happen
Social withdrawal and self-isolation due to fear of judgment, weakening external support
Persistent sadness and meaning dilemmas brought by pet-loss grief, triggering and maintaining the current problem
Avoiding creation and interrupted daily self-care, further lowering Self-efficacy

antecedent: Mistakes appearing in creation or feeling not perfect enough
When thinking of commemorating the deceased dog with a perfect work
target_behavior.core_reason: Seeing imperfection as total failure (black-and-white/catastrophizing), and worrying about being judged by others; grief after losing the pet heightens sensitivity to failure
target_behavior.function: Avoiding Anxiety and shame, avoiding outside judgment and self-disappointment
target_behavior.consequence: Significantly reduced art output, Daily routines and self-care disrupted, less joy in creation

antecedent: Finding flaws in the work or a gap from the ideal
Self-set high standards not yet met
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected 'should/must' rules tied to self-worth, negating positive experiences, persistent Self-deprecation
target_behavior.function: Trying to maintain control and drive perfect performance through self-pressure
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood, Worsening sense of failure, damaged creative motivation and process experience

antecedent: When communicating with friends or thinking others may evaluate the work
When facing situations of showing or discussing one's work
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalization and predicting others' negative evaluations (fearing being looked down on and judged)
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential criticism and shame, maintaining a surface sense of safety
target_behavior.consequence: Interpersonal tension, worsening Loneliness and pain, difficulty gaining support and feedback
